Several 2026 comparison pages cover Linear alternatives, and their pricing figures disagree, so verify before deciding.

- **Jira:** Sources describe it as the enterprise incumbent. One lists its strength as deep customization for large engineering organizations, with Standard around $7.91/user/mo and Premium around $14.54/user/mo. Another gives $8.15/user/month for Standard, and its critique is that the UI looks dated compared to Linear, Height, and Shortcut.

Other alternatives that appear across the lists include ClickUp, Asana, monday.com, and GitHub Projects. Note that the Plane blog post is written by Plane itself, so treat its comparisons with that in mind. Prices differ between sources, and one review notes that packaging in this category changes often, so confirm current pricing on each vendor's site.

I ran two searches. Linear and Jira have plenty of 2026 comparisons; ClickUp and GitHub Issues are covered only briefly.

**Linear vs. Jira:** The sources frame these as opposite philosophies. Linear uses fixed workflow states and favors speed, while Jira lets teams configure custom workflows, which one source says requires significant setup and maintenance. Reviewers generally rate Linear higher on speed and onboarding, and Jira higher on customization, reporting, enterprise permissions, and Atlassian ecosystem integrations. One source reports that Linear counts over 10,000 engineering teams, and Atlassian reports more than 250,000 Jira-family customers.

**Pricing:** The sources disagree. One lists Linear Standard at $8/user/month and Jira Standard at $7.75, another lists Linear Basic at $10 and Jira Standard at $7.91, and a third lists Linear at $8 and Jira at $7.16. Verify current prices on each vendor's site before deciding.

**ClickUp:** Coverage is thin. One listicle describes it as a broad, general-purpose tool that Linear users often move away from for speed reasons, but I found no detailed 2026 comparison.

**GitHub Issues/Projects:** One 2026 source says GitHub Projects has improved considerably and that its tight integration with pull requests and Actions is a strong advantage for teams already on GitHub. Another source calls it the default for teams that live in GitHub.

**Bottom line:** Linear suits fast-moving product engineering teams, Jira suits large or regulated organizations, and GitHub suits teams already centered on GitHub. I found no solid 2026 head-to-head data for ClickUp, so a targeted search would be needed if it's a serious candidate.

content.text:
Linear's main competitors, based on 2026 comparison pages, are below. Prices vary a lot between sources, so check each vendor's site before deciding.

| Competitor | Positioning vs. Linear | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Jira** | The enterprise incumbent. It has deeper customization, reporting, permissions and Atlassian integrations. | Linear is faster and easier to adopt. Jira's custom workflows take real setup and upkeep. Standard is about $7–8/user/month, and Linear Standard is about $8–10. |
| **Shortcut** | A lighter, story-based tracker for product and engineering teams. | Its integration library is thinner than Jira's or ClickUp's. SSO and advanced analytics need the $12 Business tier. |
| **Height** | An AI-focused tracker. | Paid plans are listed at $6 to $9.90/user/month, depending on the source. |
| **Plane** | An open-source tracker you can self-host. | It starts at about $6/seat/month and has a usable free tier. |
| **GitHub Issues/Projects** | The default for teams that already work in GitHub. | It integrates tightly with pull requests and Actions. One source says Projects has improved considerably. |
| **ClickUp, Asana, monday.com** | Broad, general-purpose work management tools. | One listicle says Linear users sometimes leave ClickUp for speed. I found no solid head-to-head comparison for it. |

**Summary:** Linear suits fast-moving product engineering teams. Jira suits large or regulated organizations. GitHub fits teams centered on GitHub. Plane fits teams that want self-hosting.

**Caveats:**
- The Plane blog post comes from a competitor, so its comparisons may be slanted.
- I only saw search summaries, not the full pages.
